relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.role: Professor of Comparative Studies in Religion
relations.evidence: Before retiring, she was Professor of Comparative Studies in Religion at the University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: In 1974 Gross was named the head of Women and Religion, a newly created section of the American Academy of Religion.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: She earned her PhD in 1975 from the University of Chicago in History of Religions

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: In 1977 Gross took refuge with Chögyam Trungpa Rinpoche, becoming a Tibetan Buddhist.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: In 2005 she was made a lopön (Tibetan (Wylie): slob dpon; Sanskrit (IAST): ācārya, "senior teacher") by Jetsün Khandro Rinpoche

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: and taught at Jetsun Khandro Rinpoche's Lotus Garden Center, located in the United States.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: Religious Feminism and the Future of the Planet: A Buddhist-Christian-Feminist Conversation (with Rosemary Radford Ruether), New York: Continuum, 2001.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: Editor (with Terry Muck): Christians Talk About Buddhist Meditation: Buddhists Talk About Christian Prayer; New York: Continuum, 2003.

relations.subject: Rita M. Gross
relations.evidence: Editor (with Nancy A. Falk): Unspoken Worlds: Women's Religious Lives; Belmont, CA: Wadsworth Press, 1989
